lesson.title: The Famous Irregulars
lesson.subtitle: fui/fue (shared by ser and ir!), hice/hizo (hacer), tuve/tuvo (tener) in past narratives

hook.title: One Preterite for Two Verbs: Why Ser and Ir Both Become 'Fui / Fue'!
hook.content: Here is one of history's wildest linguistic mergers: in Latin, the verb 'to go' (īre) became so worn down in the past tense that speakers borrowed the past tense of 'to be' (Latin fuī 'I was') whenever they meant 'I went' ('I was to the market' = 'I went to the market')! As a result, ser ('to be') and ir ('to go') have 100% IDENTICAL forms in the preterite: yo fui ('I was / I went'), tú fuiste ('you were / you went'), él/ella/usted fue ('he/she/it was OR went')!

pattern.title: How Context Separates 'It Was' from 'He Went'
pattern.content: Followed by a destination with a/al (Fue al restaurante, Fui a Madrid), fue/fui means 'went'. Followed by an adjective or noun (Fue fantástico, Fue un éxito), fue means 'was'!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:
exercises.target_answer: fue, comí, fue al restaurante, fue fantástico, fue un éxito
exercises.meaning: he/she/it was (ser) OR went (ir), I ate (comer), he went to the restaurant, it was fantastic, it was a success

exercises.prompt: What does 'Fue a Madrid y fue fantástico' mean?
options: He/she went to Madrid and it was fantastic
He goes to Madrid and it is fantastic
It was Madrid and he went fantastic
exercises.target_answer: He/she went to Madrid and it was fantastic
exercises.meaning: He/she went to Madrid and it was fantastic
exercises.explanation: The first fue (before a Madrid) is ir ('went'); the second fue (before fantástico) is ser ('was')!

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'Yesterday he went to the restaurant'
exercises.meaning: Yesterday he went to the restaurant

exercises.idea: say that the reservation was a success

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Ayer fue al hotel y comí allí
exercises.target_answer: Ayer fue al hotel y comí allí
exercises.meaning: Yesterday he went to the hotel and I ate there
cues: and I ate there: y comí allí
exercises.explanation: Ayer fue al hotel y comí allí.

summary.outcome: Deploy fue as the shared preterite of both ser ('was') and ir ('went').

use_example.german: Ayer fue a Madrid y la visita fue un éxito.
use_example.english: Yesterday he/she went to Madrid and the visit was a success.

summary.takeaway: ser and ir share the exact same preterite (fui, fuiste, fue) — 'a + place' tells you it means 'went'!
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([19] The Imperfect: The Storytelling Past): paint ongoing past scenes and habits with -aba, -ía, era, and estaba.

twist.explanation: Fue un éxito ('It was a success').

fue.english_cognate: was / went (shared preterite of ser & ir!)
fue.shift_rule: Shared preterite of ser and ir (fui, fuiste, fue)
fue.etymology_derivation: ser ('to be') and ir ('to go') share the exact same preterite forms: fui ('I was / I went'), fue ('it was / he went')!

ser.etymology_derivation: Ser describes what something is: identity, origin, inherent nature. Latin esse fused with sedēre ('to sit/settle').

ir.context_translation: I am going to go tomorrow.
ir.etymology_derivation: Latin īre ('to go', preserved in English exit 'go out' and transit 'go across')!

hacer.context_translation: I want to make a reservation.
hacer.etymology_derivation: Latin facere shifted initial f- to silent h- in Spanish: hacer. English keeps the f in fact and factory.

tener.etymology_derivation: Latin tenēre ('to hold'). While other tongues used 'have' (like French avoir), Spanish promoted 'hold' (tener) to main possession.

comí.context_translation: Yesterday I ate at that restaurant.
